cells.verb: letting yourself be moved before you've decided what you feel
cells.place: on the way to a goal you've chosen
cells.ask: let one thing you don't have a verdict on yet land anyway — without filing it, without renaming it, without turning it into a next step. Leave the knowing open, and it keeps deepening.
cells.core:
You're moving toward something and staying open at the same time — which is the hard part. Most people who are going somewhere close the doors as they go, so nothing can reach them at speed. You've kept one open. Something can still get in, and that's not hesitation in you; it's the thing that keeps the direction honest.

You don't have to know what you feel before you're allowed to feel it. You're already receiving while you walk.
cells.sheetLine: You're moving, and still open to being changed on the way.

cells.tense: bracing at a future that can't be written in yet — ahead of yourself
cells.verb: trying to feel it all in advance
cells.place: on a road you've already mapped to the end
cells.ask: take one thing you've already decided how it goes, and let the deciding wait. Put it down unfinished on purpose. The clarity you want comes after the choosing, not before.
cells.core:
You've gotten ahead of your own life. Attempting to pre-empt every feeling, every outcome, what hasn't happened yet, so when it arrives there's no room left in you — you already rehearsed it, dealt with it, moved past it. The wanting to be ready is doing the work of being somewhere; you're standing over a road and you're not on it.

The takeaway: choosing from clarity is fine. Choosing from compulsion to have everything settled in advance is what's exhausting you.
cells.sheetLine: You're holding the outcome before you've had the moment.

cells.tense: standing at a door that's already behind you — past-anchored
cells.place: at the edge of a goal you stopped moving toward
cells.ask: pick something small and be brand new at it. Not to finish anything — just to meet it with no plan, no history, no folder. Presence, not effort. The direction finds you when you're standing in front of something with nothing already true about it.
cells.core:
You aimed at something and somewhere back there the receiving stopped. Not the wanting — that may still be around — but the letting-it-in. You can still point at the goal; you just can't be reached on the way to it. Whatever happened, the openness closed first and the walking got heavier after.

What's missing isn't effort. It's being available to what's actually in front of you, fresh, without the plan already loaded.
cells.sheetLine: You're still pointed at it. You just can't be reached anymore.

cells.tense: pen down in a room you're already writing — the reach is live, the claim isn't
cells.place: inside a goal you'd say you're just pushing through
cells.ask: name one thing you already know — not what you've concluded, what you see — and say 'I noticed that' about it. Let it be enough that it landed. It was accurate before you named it; you're just signing for it now.
cells.core:
You're already open. Things reach you — you get that hit of knowing before the argument starts, you're moved by something and then you keep calling it just how you get through the work. The opening is running the whole time. You're the last one in the room to hear about it.

You don't have to defend what you noticed. It landed on its own.
cells.sheetLine: You already received it. You just haven't caught yourself.
